name: Twisted Fate
notes: Destiny (R) is cast once at t=0 purely so it registers as an ability activation for on-cast item effects; it deals no damage of its own and its Gate recast is a pure repositioning blink with no offensive value against a stationary dummy, so it is never recast.

Pick a Card (W) is cast on cooldown: the initial cast has no cast time and only counts as an ability activation (no damage), and it is always followed by a recast on the Blue Card, the highest single-target damage option, rather than Red or Gold.

The wait before recasting on Blue Card is assumed to average 0.5 s, the mean of the 0 / 0.5 / 1.0 s delay to reach Blue depending on which of the three cards happens to be hovered first when the cycle starts.

The recast resets Twisted Fate's attack timer and arms his next basic attack with a 0.25 s cast time that deals Blue Card's own magic damage instead of normal AD damage; that attack cannot critically strike but its damage is boosted by a flat fraction of crit chance instead. This is modeled by zeroing the attack's own AD for that swing (via attack_damage) and dealing Blue Card's damage separately once it lands.
Wild Cards (Q) is cast on cooldown for its magic damage.

Stacked Deck (E) generates a stack on every landed basic attack, including an empowered Pick a Card attack, up to 3; the following attack then consumes the stacks for bonus magic damage. The sources do not say the two on-hit effects are mutually exclusive, so both are allowed to land on the same swing if their timing coincides.
Twisted Fate auto-attacks continuously between casts, both to build Stacked Deck stacks and to deliver the Pick a Card recast's empowered attack.
Mana is not modeled: nothing here binds inside a 15 s fight at level 16.

assumed.why: average delay to hover Blue Card given a random starting card among Blue/Red/Gold cycling every 0.5s; the sim deterministically always recasts on Blue so a fixed average wait stands in for the random start
